purpose: Bounded matched isolated headless Chrome comparison of OBrush0.1.3 browser lag and final0.1.4; normal continuous/crossing Draw and a separate pending Save/history barrier check.
claim_scope: Actual WASM/WebGL2 headless host and synthetic pointer dispatch; this is neither physical human input-to-photon latency, a guaranteed FPS target, native GUI certification nor ZBrush parity.

method.ownership: Only spawned headless Chrome processes, dedicated isolated profiles, owned loopback HTTP/CDP listeners; no visible window, desktop/accessibility, user tabs or user Chrome process control. Only loopback page requests allowed.
method.initial_document: Fresh level-6 sphere,40,962vertices/81,920triangles; Draw,radius0.180,strength0.35,Xsymmetrytrue,noinvert,defaultcamera. Orbit check uses right drag then reloads before all sculpt measurements.
method.timing: Node sends independent fixed schedules without awaiting individual CDP acknowledgements. Phases include input and an observed drain interval: all acknowledgements, >250ms since last DOM pointer and mesh buffer upload, last callback <50ms. Save/undo/redo/serialization and screenshots are excluded from normal measured phases.
method.drain_limit: This is an observed inactivity heuristic, not direct inspection of the private Rust queue. Subsequent save/history and the separate pending-command check establish completed edits and command ordering.
method.statistics: Sort finite samples ascending; pX is element floor((n-1)*X). Null maximum denotes no samples, not an observed zero duration.
method.raf: Independent scheduling pump and app rAF callback timings; idle pump runs even when no mesh frame is submitted. No idle rendering FPS claim.
method.long_tasks: PerformanceObserver longtask entries (>50ms) whose start falls within the measured phase.
method.mesh_submissions: WebGL drawElements(TRIANGLES) count>=200000, selecting these 81k+triangle meshes. Raw harness geometry_draws also includes some egui draws with count>10000; comparison recomputes mesh counts instead of using raw geometry_frames.
method.mesh_submission_intervals: CPU timestamps between actual mesh drawElements submissions, not GPU completion/presentation. Crossing max intervals include the intentional200ms inter-stroke pause.
method.webgl_timers: CPU duration of large bufferData calls and getParameter/isEnabled; these are instrumented submission/possible-stall times, not independent GPU timer queries or total GPU transfer/render cost.
method.input_timers: DOM handling minus event timestamp and CDP acknowledgement minus send time include synthetic dispatch/browser/IPC scheduling; no hardware pen/mouse latency claim.
method.instrumentation_overhead: Both baseline and final use the exact same instrumented harness; instrumentation overhead, headless behavior, OS load and thermal variation remain.

scheduler_contract: FIFO captured world rays, brush settings and delta with ordered Begin/End history markers; at most2dabs/frame,8ms checked between atomic dabs, repaint requested until queue empty. An individual dab can exceed8ms. Commands and starting Move synchronously flush pending work; Save latency with a large backlog is demonstrated separately below.

pending_command_barrier.status: completed same-frame release and command barrier smoke
pending_command_barrier.limits: Separate8-zigzag burst plus final250px segment and mouseup/Save real button sent as one non-awaited CDP batch. No app rAF callback occurs between sculpt mouseup and Save release. Independent quiet control retains the same final segment. Aggregate longtask timings include synchronous pending-work flush, save and history, unlike normal timing phases. Save equals later quiet Save and independent quiet control; whole stroke Undo restores fresh sphere; exact Redo restores save.

limits: Two bounded trials on one Apple M2, one Chrome version, ANGLE Metal and DPR1 only.
No nativeGUI, Safari/Firefox, alternate GPU/backend, DPR scaling/resize/context-loss, imported large meshes, long sessions, pressure/tablet or physical input/presentation measurements in this update.
Normal rAF cadence and mesh submissions improve; this does not establish hard real-time frame budgets or a maximum sculpt capacity.
Fast input can build a pending queue; individual atomic dabs and synchronous command flush can still take longer than their nominal per-frame budget.
Public file-picker/load/OBJ/persistence paths are not exercised by this performance harness; save uses the actual public browser download callback captured locally.
No commercial reference app was compared for these performance measurements; feature parity remains governed by docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md.

The input adapter samples aggregate pointer state; multiple raw paths/strokes in a frame, a new stroke on pending expanded geometry, and mid-drag commands without a release remain coverage gaps. FIFO retention covers accepted dabs; captured primary release protects the active prior-frame endpoint before commands.
